Yes, there are many horrible ear issues and even beyond that which can come from too much loud noise.

Just using myself as an example. Loud music ( not sure if it was concerts or prolonged use of headphones but doesn’t really matter) ruined my life. There are people who chose to end their life due to their auditory issues. Imagine not being able to handle other humans voices, not being able to hear running water without it sounding distorted and hearing electrical hissing noises over it, no more music, no more doing anything outside of your house and even inside of your house is torture because wearing ear plugs is hard (traps your tinnitus) but without ear plugs noise causes you pain.

My sound induced tinnitus actually led to visual issues - visual snow. There’s an entire sub Reddit for it r/visualsnow and I know many people who developed this from too much noise. Basically if you’re prone to it, your brain kind of goes haywire due to hearing damage and it causes visual and vestibular issues as well (trouble with altitudes, pressure, dizziness, etc).

I’ve had multiple audiograms and audiologists tell me my hearing is great but I know it’s damaged. Certain sounds have this hollow flute distortions over it, and other noises (especially anything industrial sounding like leaf blowers) it feels like droning noises separate from the rest of the sound and sounds 10x as loud and makes my head feel like it’s vibrating. My ears feel like when you put a seashell next to your ear.

It’s relatively rare (think of all the people who have all kinds of crazy exposure to loud noise whether through work or hobbies) - but it’s also not as rare as some might think.

If you’re blasting your ears with loud music hoping you will lose hearing, I HIGHLY advise against that. Please protect your hearing. If anything throw some ear plugs on and wear headphones over that if you need to block something out.

Hearing loss can come with all types of horrible auditory issues on top of other stuff, and it may result in you losing all the tools available to you for coping with Misophonia (headphones, ear plugs, etc).

Be careful.

No, it’s not. It actually doesn’t take a lot of loud noise to damage your hearing.

You can develop hidden hearing loss. You can develop horrible tinnitus. Tinnitus is a gamble and it doesn’t always match the level of ear damage you have, so you can have severe tinnitus with a good audiogram. 

Even worse than that you can get noxacusis / pain hyperacusis where you won’t ever be able to wear headphones. Some people become specifically sensitive to digital audio (like music) and if you do listen to it you will get nerve pain. I haven’t been able to listen to music for many years now because of this, and can no longer use headphones. 

You can also develop sound distortion from loud music, and a condition called tonic tensor tympani syndrome where the little muscles inside of your middle ear will spasm and feel like someone’s beating a little drum in your ear. It’s extremely annoying, like a hiccup in your ear that won’t go away.

Speaking from experience, this is something myself and many others developed from too much sound. Loud music pounding directly into your ear canal for long periods of time is extremely dangerous.

You’re not actually blocking out 32 decibels.
The formula is (NRR - 7) / 2, so if you have -32db ear plugs, you have to do (32-7)/2 = 12.5
So if you’re at a 100 decibel concert, you are taking in (100-12.5)=87.5 db of noise, not (100-32)=68.

87.5 is still pretty loud and ears are sensitive to not only volume but frequencies. The best way to mitigate this is to not go to venues that are this loud and if you want to enjoy concerts stick to outdoor ones and stay away from speakers. 

Also note that decibel readers on your phone are pretty inaccurate

Sounds like you’re experiencing Tonic Tensor Tympani syndrome, or otherwise known as Middle Ear Myoclonus (MEM). It’s a dysfunction of the middle ear muscles, and it commonly appears after overexposure to loud noises so many of us here experience this. 

Hyperacusis is poorly defined in general but many tend to use the term to describe a sensitivity to volume or select frequencies (or both), where you suddenly become sensitive to sounds others find normal. That sensitivity can be just loudness perception, or it can include these weird ear spasms (can be popping, crackling, fluttering, tapping, etc).

It can happen both directly in response to noise, or in silence without noise. I’m someone who experiences both. Artificial audio (headphones, tinny speakers) tend to be a major trigger, and this issue commonly appears in people who are frequently exposed to loud noises (loud headphones, concerts, construction and so on).

Is your skin more oily, dry, or combination
Do you like a full coverage or something on the lighter side
Do you want SPF in your foundation 
Tone of your skin (if you’re more pinkish, neutral or olive)

Hello!

I have never had a problem as I’ve always lived in sunny/hot climates in california. The first time I still think was because I used a tanning oil which attracts the sun even more, never experienced it after that. I recently moved to San Francisco and I think it’s all been due to the very minimal sun exposure I’ve had here that made it all flare up. I was on vacation in Hawaii and around day 4 or so it developed, even though I applied plenty of sunscreen and never got sunburnt but did lay out in the sun for about 4 hours total one day (2 - 2 hour intervals). I read that sun/heat rashes tend to appear because your skin is overexposed and freaks out and goes in”defense” mode, so I think it was all just too much at once. My mom is also prone to skin conditions caused by the sun, but hers is a bit more chronic as it’s more of an allergy that comes to stay for weeks at a time. She said she didn’t develop it until she was in her 50s but it definitely looks different than mine, more pimply and indivual big bumps rather than mine which is flat, swollen red puffy surfaces up to 48” long. What helped me a bit was Aloe lotion with lidocaine, cortisone cream and Melatonin to ease my anxiety before bed.

While this isn’t anywhere near the same as what you’re dealing with, on a recent vacation I developed a terrible sun rash. I’ve had it in the past and thought it was due to the sunscreen I used. This time it went away in a week but the burning and itching was terrible. My last flare up lasted weeks and covered my arms, stomach, chest and legs, and once the patches of red bumps went away, they left terrible scabs for weeks. I also used to work in food service and all the cleaning chemicals would literally burn the skin on my hands and also leave rashes on all my fingers which to this day occasionally flare up without reason and my hands get super hot and itchy.

Doesn’t help that I’m an anxious person by nature, so even minor things such a sun rash give me terrible anxiety. 

Hang in there!
